newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Croatia kicks off debut Eurobond roadshow in HK.
newsitem.headline: Croatia kicks off debut Eurobond roadshow in HK.

text.p: Croatia kicked off an extensive roadshow for its debut Eurobond in Hong Kong with hopes of tapping into Asia's growing investor base, finance minister Bozo Prka said on Monday.
"We like the way (Asia) is doing business and that it is very market oriented," Prka told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.
The Asian market shows good prospects, especially for Middle and East European countries, he said, "because investors appreciate stable economies and growth".

Croatia plans to launch a US$250 million five-year Eurobond following a whirlwind global roadshow that will travel from Asia to the United States and then onto Europe. The final presentation will be in London on February 5.
Merrill Lynch and Union Bank of Switzerland are joint lead managers for the deal.
In Asia, presentations will be made in Hong Kong, Tokyo and Seoul.

In presenting Croatia's case, Prka said he would highlight macroeconomic stablity, healthy growth, low inflation, a low fiscal deficit, increasing reserves and improved political stability in the wake of a 1995 peace settlement following four years of war.

"We have low indebtedness of 25 percent of GDP (gross domestic product), a debt service ratio of between five and 10 percent and net foreign indebtedness of only three percent of our exports," he said.

Prka said Croatia grew 6.5 percent in real terms in 1996 while inflation was 3.5 percent. "We expect the same rate of growth in the coming period of time and that is a good story to be told to Asian investors," he said.
Prka said Croatia is "moderately exposed" to a fiscal deficit. "Last year it was one percent (of GDP) and this year it will be 2.5 percent," he said.
He estimated gross borrowing requirments for 1997 at US$1 billion. "We are looking at longer-term borrowings with maturities of between five and seven years," said Prka.
He said Croatia would start with U.S. dollar and German mark denominated Eurobonds, but may issue bonds in Japan's samurai and the U.S. yankee bond markets in the future.
